_comment: Outbound IP telephony — call events, the consent gate, the outbound queue and the retention window (P14 stages A and B / T4). This block declares what the platform needs in order to read a call log and answer three questions honestly: may we call this number, for this purpose, and may we record it; at what pace may we call at all; and how long may we hold the record. It declares nothing that could place a call, and nothing that could carry audio. Copy the 'telephony' block below into config/integrations.json, merged under the tenant key next to 'sheets_registers', 'assets' and 'business_graph'. Every register and range named here must already exist in that tenant's sheets_registers block. Replace SET_... values before use.
_note_no_audio: Audio never reaches the platform. There is no configuration key, tool argument or output field that carries a recording, a recording URL, a transcript, a PCM buffer or a media path. The register this block reads is an operator-written CALL LOG, not a media store. If a column the operator points at happens to hold a locator (a scheme-prefixed URL, or a cell ending in a media extension such as .wav/.mp3/.opus), that cell is WITHHELD and counted in 'withheld_outcomes' rather than republished as a call outcome — because 'treat the column as opaque text' is exactly how a recording link leaks into a model's context and from there to a third party. This boundary is measured by scripts/probes/probe_telephony_consent.py, not promised here.
_note_directions: direction_column must hold 'inbound' or 'outbound' (case-insensitive). 'inbound' means the customer called us — they opened the contact, so the outbound consent question does not apply. 'outbound' means we called them, which is the direction that requires a declared consent. A row whose direction is neither is skipped and counted in 'skipped', never guessed as inbound to avoid the gate.
_note_purposes: purpose is declared PER REGISTER and must be one of: service, delivery, payment, support, marketing. It is not read from a column, because a row that could relabel itself could relabel a marketing call as a service call to pass a gate. A consent to call about a delivery is NOT a consent to call about a promotion, and collapsing them into one flag is how a lawful list becomes an unlawful one. If a tenant runs campaigns and service calls, they get two registers with two purposes and two consent rows per number.
_note_consent_is_declaration: The 'consent_registers' block points at the register where the operator records consent, one row per (number, purpose). Only two statuses exist: 'granted' and 'withdrawn'. There is no 'pending' and no 'unknown', because a consent whose state is neither of these is a record we cannot read — and reading it as granted is the defect this whole block exists against. An unreadable status or an unreadable purpose lands in 'unreadable_consent_rows' and grants nothing.
_note_expiry: expiry_column is optional. When declared and a row carries a date, a consent past that date is treated as withdrawn with the reason 'expired' rather than 'missing', so the operator is sent to the right fix. A date cell that is not an ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) is counted as unreadable and grants nothing: a consent whose end date cannot be read is a consent the platform cannot honour, and treating it as open-ended would be a guess.
_note_recording: recording_column is optional and records whether the customer consented to the call being RECORDED. That is a separate consent from the call itself under the PRD's VO-07. When it is absent, or its cell does not say yes, 'recording_allowed' is false. This is deliberately NOT the same as 'no recording exists' — the platform does not know whether a recording exists, and it must not read the absence of permission as evidence about the recording.
_note_numbers: consented_numbers is the operator's allowlist of numbers that may be called at all. It is OPTIONAL, and the distinction between an empty list and an absent key matters: an absent key means 'no allowlist is declared' and is reported as allowlist_declared: false with the other checks still applying; a present but empty list is a list that admits nothing. Every number is compared as DIGITS ONLY (+998 90 123 45 67 and 998-90-123-45-67 are one number), and matched by exact equality, never by prefix: a prefix match would call a stranger because a shorter number was consented. A number that is not a usable phone number (a name, a blank, an over-long run of digits) is refused at configure time, not silently ignored.
_note_refusal: Calling a number with no declaration is REFUSED IN CODE, by name, not by a prompt. An outbound call to someone who did not consent is a legal problem, not a quality problem, and a rule that lives only in a model's instructions is a rule a convincing input can remove. telephony.consent is a read tool that answers the question 'may we call this number, and may we record it'; an unknown number yields consented: false WITH A REASON rather than an exception, because the caller asking 'may I call' needs the answer 'no' to be usable.
_note_blank_vs_zero: A blank cell is 'not recorded' and a cell holding text is 'unreadable'; neither becomes zero and neither becomes a number. A call with no readable duration has duration_seconds: null, and a duration total is always shown beside its 'timed_count', so a sum over two calls can never be mistaken for a sum over two hundred. An unreadable duration is None, never 0.
_note_person: No per-person figure exists and no configuration key could create one. There is no agent_column, operator_column, per-agent count, rank, rating or leaderboard; a count of calls is a fact about a telephone line, while a count of calls per agent is a number that will be used in a review, and the platform does not know why a call was long or short. An extension column may be declared and is reported only as a bound ASSET path, never as a person. This is asserted structurally by the test suite and measured by scripts/probes/probe_telephony_consent.py.
_note_readonly: All five tools are read-only: telephony.consent, telephony.call_events, telephony.summary, telephony.queue, telephony.retention. Placing a call is deliberately NOT a tool — it would be an outbound write to a person, and the consent gate must be enforced by code on the one path that can reach a provider, not by a prompt on a path any agent could hold. Every read goes through sheets.rows, so the register declaration, A1 allowlist, agent tool permission and connection allowlist all apply unchanged. This module adds no transport and no new authority.
_note_window: Call logs are continuous, so every read is WINDOWED and LIMITED. since/until are ISO dates compared as text against the register's own cell (parsing ambiguous formats such as 10.01.2026 would silently include or exclude the wrong day), and limit is bounded. 'truncated' always ships: a manager who sees a partial list must be told it is partial.
_note_throughput: throughput declares the pace at which outbound calling may lawfully proceed: 'per_window' calls per 'window_seconds'. It is OPTIONAL, and its absence is the safe default — a tenant with no declared pace has ZERO capacity, so every callable row is reported as over_capacity and none is described as callable. An operator who has not decided their pace has not decided to call anyone. When declared, the ceiling is ENFORCED and not merely reported: if the read finds more callable rows than the pace could carry, the surplus is counted in 'over_capacity' and is not presented as callable. A queue that overstates what may be called is worse than a short one, because the remedy for a short list is to wait and the remedy for an overstated list is nothing. The pace is bounded (window at least 60 seconds, at most 86,400; at most 1000 per window), because a total rather than a rate would permit a burst no human could supervise.
_note_retention: retention_days declares how long a call record may be held, and is REQUIRED whenever a consent register is declared. A tenant that records consent to call people has thereby declared that it holds personal data about them, and a data holder with no retention window has made the choice VO-07 forbids by omission — so it is refused at configure time, not defaulted. The window is finite and positive: 'keep forever' is not a retention policy, it is the absence of one. The platform NEVER deletes a call record: telephony.retention is a REPORT, not an act. It states per row whether the operator's own declared window has passed, so the decision to destroy and the act of destroying both stay with the operator, who is the only party that can show a lawful basis. Every row lands in exactly one of three states — 'in_window', 'past_window' or 'unaged' — and 'unaged' is deliberately not folded into either of the others: a row whose date cannot be read must never be expired by accident, because a typo in a date must not license destroying evidence.
_note_queue: telephony.queue names the numbers that COULD be called, with the consent gate already applied — it is what a later dialer would read, and that dialer must still pass through the same gate. It is not a dialer: no queue item carries a dial instruction, a transport, an audio path or a command. A row whose consent check fails is listed too, marked consented: false with its reason, because hiding an ungated row would leave an operator believing their list is clean. 'limit' bounds the ITEMS CARRIED, never the evaluation: every row is still examined, so 'matched' and 'over_capacity' describe the whole window and not just the slice the caller asked to see — 'there are 900 callable numbers' and 'here are 50 of them' are two different facts, and a caller given only the second would pace against the wrong number.
